rationale: Brings the end of DP23 into the standard shape of the DP Format Guide, without changing any text. Strong DP23 Alignment (25) and Failure Conditions (26) move into Minimum DP23 Alignment as 24.9 and 24.10, so the whole alignment bar is in one section. Initial Implementation Path (27) moves into Implementation Patterns as 20.12, next to the patterns it sequences. The Proposed Constitutional Statement (28) becomes the last lines of Closing Orientation. The chapter then ends with the six standard closing sections (22–27). The (Non-Normative) label also comes off the Section 24 heading, because the style guide says that section holds requirements.

edits.note: This section holds the chapter's alignment requirements, so the (Non-Normative) label contradicts it (style guide, Requirements; DP Format Guide 6.3).
What a strongly aligned system adds is alignment content. It becomes a subsection of Minimum DP23 Alignment instead of a section of its own (DP Format Guide 5.2, test 3). Text unchanged.
When a system must not claim alignment is alignment content. It becomes a subsection of Minimum DP23 Alignment (DP Format Guide 6.3). Text unchanged.

### 20.11 Graceful refusal
Where a community has restricted translation, indexing, or summarization, render an explicit notice of restriction rather than an empty result, so that absence is legible rather than mistaken for silence.

## 28. Proposed Constitutional Statement
> No person’s ability to participate in collective sensemaking should depend on the language they speak. The Meta-Layer must preserve original expression, enable understanding across languages, make machine interpretation visible and contestable, protect cultural and contextual integrity, and show how participation influences shared understanding and action.
edits.note: Deleted from here: the statement moves to the end of Closing Orientation (see the edit below).

edits.original_text: It should enable humanity’s many voices to become mutually legible, collectively navigable, and meaningfully connected to responsibility and action.
edits.proposed_text:
It should enable humanity’s many voices to become mutually legible, collectively navigable, and meaningfully connected to responsibility and action.

DP23 proposes this statement for the Meta-Layer’s constitution:

> No person’s ability to participate in collective sensemaking should depend on the language they speak. The Meta-Layer must preserve original expression, enable understanding across languages, make machine interpretation visible and contestable, protect cultural and contextual integrity, and show how participation influences shared understanding and action.
edits.note: The proposed constitutional statement is the chapter's closing line rather than a section of its own; Core Principle already holds the principle statement (DP Format Guide 3.4, 6.6). Quote unchanged.
